text: One day, a boy named Tim found a hat. It was not a regular hat. It was big and red. Tim put the hat on his head. Tim walked to the park. He saw a cat. The cat said, "Nice hat, Tim!" Tim smiled and said, "Thank you, cat!" Then, the wind began to blow. The hat flew off Tim's head. The wind struck the hat high into a tree. Tim was sad. The cat climbed the tree and got the hat. Tim was happy again. They played together all day.

One day, a nice cat and a little dog were playing in the park. They were best friends. The sun was shining and they were very happy. The cat found a ball under a palm tree. The dog wanted to play with the ball too. The cat said, "I will lend you the ball, but you have to give it back." The little dog agreed and they started to play. After a while, the little dog did not want to give the ball back to the cat. The cat said, "You promised to give it back. Please give it back now." The little dog felt bad and gave the ball back to the cat. They both learned to share and play together nicely.

Once upon a time, there was a huge tree in a park. Under the tree, there was some colorful chalk. A little boy named Tim found the chalk and wanted to play with it. Tim started to draw on the ground with the chalk. He drew a big sun, a house, and some flowers. Tim was very happy with his drawings. He smiled and laughed as he drew with the chalk. Then, it was time for Tim to leave the park. He took the chalk and put it back under the huge tree. Tim waved goodbye to his drawings and walked away. He knew that he could come back to the park and play with the chalk again another day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to climb. She climbed on chairs, on trees, and on her bed. One day, Lily saw a big hill. She thought it would be perfect to climb. Lily started to climb the big hill. She climbed and climbed until she was very high. Then, she saw something on the top of the hill. It was a big muffin! Lily was very happy. She loved muffins. But when Lily got to the top of the hill, she saw that the muffin was not real. It was just a big rock that looked like a muffin. Lily was sad, but then she saw her mom coming up the hill. Her mom had a real, yummy muffin just for Lily. They sat on the big rock and ate the perfect muffin together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He loved to play outside in the dirt. One day, Tim found a big, dirty rock in his yard. He thought it was fun to push the rock around and make it roll. As Tim pushed the rock, something strange happened. The rock cracked open! Inside the rock, he found a small, shiny box. Tim was very surprised. He had never seen anything like this before. Tim opened the box and found a note. The note said, "The truth is, you are a great helper!" Tim felt happy and proud. He knew that even though he was dirty from playing, he had found something special. The unexpected truth made Tim feel like he could do anything.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tom. He loved to play in the kitchen with his mom. They would make easy and yummy treats together. Tom's favorite treat to make was cookies. One day, Tom's mom said, "Tom, let's make cookies together!" Tom was so happy. He put on his apron and helped his mom get all the things they needed. They mixed the dough and rolled it out. Then, they cut out fun shapes with their cookie cutters. When the cookies were ready, Tom and his mom shared them with the family. Everyone loved the cookies and said they were the best they ever had. Tom felt proud and happy. From that day on, Tom and his mom made cookies in the kitchen all the time.

Once upon a time, there was a little dove. The dove liked to whistle. One day, the dove met a big bird. The big bird had a harsh voice. The big bird did not like the dove's whistle. The big bird told the dove, "Stop your whistle! I don't like it!" The dove felt sad. The dove did not want to stop whistling. The dove liked to whistle. The dove thought of a plan. The dove would whistle far away from the big bird. The dove flew away and found a nice tree. The dove whistled in the tree. The big bird did not hear the whistle. The dove was happy.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sarah. She was a very curious three year old who never stopped exploring! One day her parents took her to the museum. Sarah was so excited. She ran around the museum looking at all the different things. She was so restless! Suddenly Sarah found a giant pile of colorful ribbons lying at the back of the room. She asked her mum if she could play with them. Her mum said yes and she taught Sarah how to tie the ribbons together into different shapes. Sarah giggled and enjoyed trying out different patterns. When Sarah finished, she was so proud of herself. She was excited to show her parents her ribbon masterpiece. Her mum smiled and said, "That looks beautiful, Sarah!" Sarah was so happy as she hugged her mum and held her ribbon tight. She had never felt so proud before!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue loved to draw and sign her name on her art. One day, Sue made a big, pretty print of her favorite tree. She was so proud of it. She wanted to show it to her mom and dad. Sue put on her coat because it was cold outside. She walked to her mom and dad's house. On the way, something unexpected happened. A big gust of wind blew her print away! Sue was very sad and tried to catch it, but it was too fast. Then, a kind bird saw Sue's print flying away. The bird grabbed the print in its beak and brought it back to Sue. She was so happy! Sue thanked the bird and ran to her mom and dad's house. She showed them her print, and they all laughed at the funny twist in her day.

Once upon a time, there was a little red radio. The radio lived on a high shelf in a big room. Every day, the radio played fun songs for all the kids to dance to. The kids loved the red radio, but they could not reach it to change the songs. One day, a tall man came to visit the kids. The tall man saw the red radio on the high shelf. He knew the kids wanted to change the songs, but they were too small to reach it. The tall man had a plan to help the kids. The tall man went outside and found a long stick. He brought the stick inside and showed the kids how to use it. The kids took turns using the stick to reach the red radio. They changed the songs and danced to their favorite tunes. The kids were very happy, and they thanked the tall man for helping them reach their red radio.

Once upon a time, there was a funny cat named Sam. Sam loved to supply his friends with jokes to make them laugh. One day, Sam was worried because he could not think of a new joke. Sam went to his friend, a little bird named Lily. He said, "Lily, I am worried. I can't think of a new joke to make our friends laugh. Can you help me?" Lily thought for a moment and said, "Why don't we ask our friends to help us? Maybe they have a joke we can share." Sam and Lily went to their friends, and they all shared their best jokes. Sam was no longer worried. Now, he had many jokes to supply and make everyone laugh. And they all had a fun and happy day together.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. His name was Mark and he really liked aeroplanes. One day, Mark wanted to go on an aeroplane ride with his mum and dad. But when his parents said no, Mark started to worry. "Why don't I get to go on the aeroplane?" asked Mark to his mum. "It's too dangerous," said his mum. Mark started to cry. He was so sad that he couldn't go on the aeroplane. Suddenly, Mark saw a green aeroplane flying in the sky. It was so close that he could almost touch it. Mark smiled and waved to the aeroplane. He forgot all about his worries.

Once upon a time, there was a big red ball. The ball liked to play with a little girl named Sue. Sue would kick the ball, and the ball would roll far away. Sue and the ball had lots of fun. One day, Sue kicked the ball too hard. It went into the kitchen and hit a sink. The sink was full of water. The ball fell into the water and got all wet. It was a spoiled ball now. Sue was sad, but she knew how to fix it. She took the wet ball outside to dry in the sun. The ball was happy to gain its dryness back. Sue and the ball played together again, and they were both very happy.

Once upon a time, a boy named Tim found a big, impressive rock. He liked it a lot and put it in his pocket. Tim wanted to show his friend, Sam, his new rock. So, he went to Sam's house. "Look, Sam!" said Tim. "I have a big rock in my pocket!" Sam looked at the rock and thought it was very cool. They played with the rock all day. But then, something strange happened. While they were playing, the rock vanished! Tim and Sam looked everywhere for the rock, but they could not find it. They felt very sad. The big, impressive rock was gone forever, and they never found it again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a nosy cat named Tom. Tom loved to play games with his friends. His favorite game was to mix things up. One day, Tom and his friends were playing the mixing game. They mixed toys, food, and colors. They had so much fun! But then, something unexpected happened. A big dog came to play with them. The dog was very big and very nosy too. The dog wanted to play the mixing game with Tom and his friends. They were scared of the big dog, but they let him play. The big dog started to mix things up. He mixed food with toys and colors with food. Tom and his friends were surprised. The big dog was very good at the mixing game. They all had so much fun together. In the end, Tom and his friends learned that even a big nosy dog can be a good friend and play the mixing game with them.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. Amy had many shoes that she liked to wear. But her shoes were all mixed up in a big pile. It was difficult for Amy to find the right shoe when she wanted to go outside and play. One day, Amy decided to organize her shoes. She put all the shoes in a row. She put the big shoes on one side and the small shoes on the other side. Then she put the shoes that were the same together. Now it was easy for Amy to find the right shoe when she wanted to go outside and play. Amy was very happy that she organized her shoes. She showed her mom and dad, and they were proud of her. Now, Amy could go outside and play faster because she could find the right shoe quickly. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Fin. Fin lived in a big ocean. He had many friends. They liked to swim and play together. One day, Fin and his friends saw a big, dangerous shark. They were scared. The shark said, "I want to play too!" But Fin and his friends did not want to play with the dangerous shark. They swam away very fast. The shark was sad and swam away too. Fin had an idea. He found a big leaf and cut it into a long rope. He gave one end of the rope to the shark. Fin said, "You can play with us, but you must hold this rope. That way, you won't be too close and we won't be scared." The shark agreed and held the rope. They all swam and played together, and they were all happy.

Once upon a time, there was a big whale. The whale was very creative. He liked to cook food for his friends. One day, the whale wanted to make a big meal for all his friends. He was very excited. The whale started to cook. He cooked fish, crab, and seaweed. He cooked all day long. All his friends came to eat. They were very happy. They liked the whale's food a lot. The whale was happy too. But then, something bad happened. The whale cooked too much food. The food was too hot. It started a fire. The fire burned everything. The whale and his friends were sad. They had to leave their home.

Once there was a little girl named Sarah who liked to play with her friends. One day she was walking along the beach with them when she noticed a big rock. Sarah said to her friends, "Let's see who can push the rock the farthest!" Sarah, who was very competitive, wanted to win. Her friends agreed and they each tried to push the rock as far as they could. Suddenly, thunder clapped in the sky. Sarah and her friends were frightened, so they all ran to safety. The moral of this story is to remember that it's not always important to be competitive and win. Sometimes, it's important to pay attention to your surroundings and stay safe.

Once upon a time, there was a cute dog named Spot. Spot loved to jump and play all day long. He lived in a small house with his best friend, Sam. Sam and Spot did everything together. They were very happy. One day, Spot found a big bone in the yard. He was very excited and wanted to show Sam. But when Spot went to find Sam, he was not there. Spot looked all around the house, but he could not find his friend. Just when Spot was about to give up, he heard a noise. He followed the sound and found Sam hiding behind a tree. Sam had a surprise for Spot! He had found an even bigger bone for Spot to play with. Spot was so happy and they both jumped for joy. From that day on, they shared the big bone and had even more fun together.

One day, a little bunny named Lily was playing in the woods. The sun was shining and the flowers were pink. Lily liked to spring high into the air and land on the soft grass. Lily's room was very organized. She had a place for all her toys and books. Her mom was happy because Lily always put her things away. One day, Lily found a new friend in the woods. It was a baby bird who liked to spring too. They played all day and had lots of fun. At the end of the day, Lily and the baby bird went back to their organized homes. They were happy and tired from their fun day in the woods.

One day, a little girl named Amy went to a fun place with her mom. This place had lots of toys and games for kids to play with. Amy was very happy to be there. While playing, Amy heard a loud scream. She saw a boy named Tim who was scared of a big dog. Amy wanted to help Tim, so she said, "Don't be scared, I will help you." Amy took Tim's hand and they went to find a reliable grown-up. They found Amy's mom and told her about the big dog. Amy's mom said, "That dog is not real, it's just a toy!" They all went back to see the dog, and Amy and Tim laughed when they saw it was just a toy. They played together for the rest of the day and became good friends. The unexpected toy dog helped them find a new friend in each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim who loved apples. One sunny day, Tim went to the park with his mom. He took a big, red apple with him. Tim thought apples were incredible. While playing at the park, Tim saw a squirrel. The squirrel came close to Tim and looked at his apple. Tim started to wonder if the squirrel wanted his apple. He decided to share his apple with the squirrel. Tim broke the apple in half and gave one part to the squirrel. The squirrel took the apple and ran away. But then, something unexpected happened! The squirrel came back with a shiny, gold coin. The squirrel gave the coin to Tim as a thank you for the apple. Tim was so happy and surprised. He never thought that sharing his apple with a squirrel would give him a shiny, gold coin.

Once upon a time, there was a pretty hotel. The hotel was big and had many rooms. In one room, there was a little girl named Lily and her teddy bear, Mr. Cuddles. One day, Lily and Mr. Cuddles decided to play a game. They wanted to throw a ball. Lily said, "Mr. Cuddles, let's throw the ball and see who can catch it." Mr. Cuddles nodded and smiled. Lily threw the ball to Mr. Cuddles, and he caught it. Then, Mr. Cuddles threw the ball back to Lily. They played and laughed in the pretty hotel. They had so much fun and played until it was time for bed.
Once upon a time, there was a hen who lived on a farm. One day, she met a cow. They became good friends and explored the farm together. One evening, they helped a lost little rabbit find its home.

Maya the little robot woke up in a quiet workshop full of tools. She blinked her blue eyes and rolled to the window. Outside, the city was covered in snow. Maya had never seen snow before, so she rolled out the door and into the street. In the park, a group of children were building a snowman. They waved at Maya and asked her to help. Maya used her strong arms to lift the biggest snowball onto the top. When the sun went down, the children gave Maya a red scarf to keep her warm. That night, Maya rolled back to the workshop, wearing her scarf and humming a happy tune.

A small fox named Ruby lived at the edge of a deep green forest. Every morning she hunted for berries near the river. One morning, the river was flooded and Ruby could not cross it. She sat on a rock and looked at the rushing water. A wise old turtle swam up to her. "Climb on my shell," said the turtle, "and I will carry you across." Ruby held on tightly while the turtle paddled through the waves. On the other side, they found a bush full of the sweetest berries Ruby had ever tasted. They shared the berries and laughed in the warm sun.

Leo and his grandpa went fishing on a calm blue lake. They sat in a little wooden boat and waited. Suddenly, something pulled hard on Leo's line. Leo pulled and pulled until a huge silver fish jumped out of the water. The fish looked at Leo with sad eyes. Leo decided to let it go, and the fish splashed back into the lake. When they rowed home at sunset, Grandpa told Leo he was proud of him.

There was once a lonely dragon who lived in a cave high on a mountain. The villagers below were afraid of him, and nobody ever visited. One snowy winter, a little girl named Nia got lost in the storm and climbed up to the cave to stay warm. The dragon gently breathed a small fire so she would not be cold. In the morning, the dragon flew Nia back to her village on his back. The villagers saw that the dragon was kind, and they invited him to their winter festival. That evening, the dragon lit the festival lanterns, and everyone danced together under the stars.

Sam the puppy found a muddy ball in the garden. "This is the best ball ever!" he barked. "It's so dirty," said Mia the cat. "You should wash it first." Sam shook his head and kept playing. Then it started to rain. The rain washed the ball until it was bright red again. Sam brought the shiny ball to Mia. "Look, the rain washed it for me!" Mia laughed, and they played catch until the sun came out.
Ben built a paper boat. He sailed it down the stream behind his house. The boat floated all the way to the pond, where a frog jumped on board.

In a busy city lived an old baker named Rosa. Every day she baked bread in her tiny shop. One afternoon, a hungry boy stood outside her window, looking at the cakes. Rosa invited him in and gave him a warm roll. The boy came back the next day and offered to sweep the floor. Soon the boy was helping Rosa bake, and together they made the most beautiful birthday cake for the whole street. At the street party that night, everyone cheered for Rosa and her new helper.

Captain Zoe flew her silver rocket to the moon. She bounced across the dusty craters in her space suit. Behind a big rock, she discovered a tiny green alien crying. The alien had lost its spaceship. Zoe and the alien searched the moon together and finally found the little spaceship stuck in a crater. Zoe pulled it free with a rope, and the alien hugged her before flying home to its planet. Back on Earth, Zoe looked up at the stars and smiled, knowing she had a friend far away.

Under the sea, a shy octopus named Ollie hid inside a shell all day. One day, a school of colorful fish swam by and invited him to play hide and seek. Ollie was nervous but he joined them. Ollie changed his colors to match the coral and won every round. The fish cheered for Ollie, and from then on he was never shy again.

A proud hare laughed at a slow tortoise and challenged him to a race. The race began at the old oak tree. The hare dashed far ahead while the tortoise plodded along the path. Halfway to the finish, the hare felt so sure of winning that he lay down under a shady tree and fell asleep. The tortoise kept walking, slowly and steadily, past the sleeping hare. When the hare woke up, he ran as fast as he could, but the tortoise was already crossing the finish line while the other animals cheered.

A mighty lion was sleeping in the forest when a little mouse ran across his nose. The lion woke up and caught the mouse in his huge paw. "Please let me go," squeaked the mouse, "and one day I will help you." The lion laughed, but he let the mouse go. A few days later, hunters caught the lion in a strong net. The lion roared and roared, but he could not escape. The little mouse heard him and came running. She chewed through the ropes until the lion was free. From that day on, the lion and the mouse were the best of friends.

On a hot summer day, a thirsty crow flew over the fields looking for water. At last she found a tall pitcher in a garden, but the water at the bottom was too low for her beak to reach. The clever crow picked up pebbles one by one and dropped them into the pitcher. Slowly the water rose higher and higher, until the crow could finally drink.

All summer long, a grasshopper played his fiddle and sang in the sunny meadow, while a busy ant carried grains of wheat to her nest. "Why work so hard?" asked the grasshopper. "Come and sing with me!" But the ant kept working. When winter came, the meadow was covered in snow and the grasshopper had nothing to eat. Cold and hungry, he knocked on the ant's door. The kind ant let him in and shared her food by the warm fire.
